Measured on this host's own MPSGraph and compared cell for cell by tests/backports/host/mpsgraph/run.sh in a process of its own: 9 cases over both forms and their result shapes, every cell and every shape byte-identical to the release (gather_slice checks=9 failures=0 recorded=0 over 44 cells). Three shapes the release refuses, each with its own words and each a question refusals.m asks in a process of its own: a start past the end of the axis ("start value 9 does not fit dimension size (4)"), a length that runs past it ("length value 9 does not fit within the dimension size (4) with start value (2)"), a stride of zero ("stride cannot be 0"), and a result of no elements, which the release BUILDS (the shape line prints 2x0) and then cannot make an NDArray for ("device may not be nil", MPSNDArray.mm:759). THE FIVE MODES THE RELEASE ANSWERS, each measured on this host's own MPSGraph over a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) and every one of them in the differential: MPSGraphPaddingModeConstant is the caller's constantValue written in the RESULT's own type (a constant of 99 over a float32 2x4 answers 99), MPSGraphPaddingModeZero is zero, MPSGraphPaddingModeClampToEdge repeats the nearest element of the axis (measured 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4 for one at each end of axis 1), MPSGraphPaddingModeReflect mirrors ACROSS THE EDGE of the axis - the element at index -1 is the one at index +1, measured 2, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3 for one at each end, which is neither the mirror about the last element nor one that repeats the edge - and MPSGraphPaddingModeSymmetric is the mirror that DOES repeat the edge, measured 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4. Each axis is chosen on its own, because a pad is applied to every axis at once. TWO OF THE SEVEN MODES ARE REFUSED BY THE RELEASE, with its own words, "Unsupported paddingMode", after it has built the result tensor - so MPSGraphPaddingModePeriodic and MPSGraphPaddingModeAntiPeriodic are raised where the graph is built. Each mirror also has its own REACH, and neither is "the axis's own extent": measured on this host's own MPSGraph at extents one, two and three, on the left and on the right, over every padding from one to five, a REFLECT answers up to the axis LESS ONE and a SYMMETRIC up to the axis ITSELF, and one element more of either is refused by the release's compiler with its own words, "'mps.pad' op padding values too large at axis 0, max padding is 1, got 3" (MPSGraphUtilities.mm:956), where the maximum it prints is 1 for a reflect on an axis of two and 2 for a symmetric on the same axis. The clamp, the zero and the constant answer any padding at all. A pad of a RANK OF THREE answers, and the earlier text of this row was wrong: it said the release refuses one in every mode, and that was a measurement of this repository's own question asked into the wrong shape - a destination of the OPERAND's 96 bytes where the result is a 4x5x6 of 480. Asked into a destination of the RESULT's shape a 2x3x4 of (1 ... 24) padded by one at each end of every axis answers a 4x5x6 in every mode, measured, and the clamp and the symmetric answer the same bytes there because one element of padding on an axis of two or more is where the two mirrors and the clamp agree; refusals.txt now records what the narrower destination really does, which is per mode and per rank (pad-destination-narrower-rank3-clamp is refused, pad-destination-narrower-rank3-constant and pad-destination-narrower-rank2 answer). MEASURED on this host's own MPSGraph over a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) beside one of (5, 6, 7, 8 | 50, 60, 70, 80) and one of (9, 10, 11, 12 | 90, 100, 110, 120): END TO END along the axis in the order the caller wrote them, so axis 0 of the three is a 6x4 of those three 2x4s one under another and axis 1 a 2x12 of their rows side by side, and a NEGATIVE axis counted from the end (measured: axis -2 answers what axis 0 answers and axis -1 what axis 1 answers, which is the header's own -rank <= dimension < rank). ONE operand is the identity: a 2x4 on its own is a 2x4 of its own eight values. AN EXTENT OF ONE ON THE AXIS LAID ALONG is not a broadcast but one element of the result: measured, a 1x4 of (101, 102, 103, 104) laid along axis 0 beside a 2x4 is a 3x4 of (101, 102, 103, 104 | 5, 6, 7, 8 | 50, 60, 70, 80) and not a 2x4 with the row repeated. THE OPERANDS MAY DIFFER IN LENGTH ON THAT AXIS, and the result is then neither of their lengths: measured, a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) laid along axis 1 beside a 2x1 of (5, 6) is a 2x5 of (1, 2, 3, 4, 10 | 20, 30, 40, 5, 6) - the shorter operand's region is one element of the result, which is graph-cases.m's concat-unequal-axis1. EVERY OTHER AXIS MUST HOLD THE SAME EXTENT IN EVERY OPERAND, which the header calls "broadcast compatible" and the release does not take at all: measured, a 1x4 beside a 2x4 with axis 1 the one laid along is refused by its own compiler with "'mps.concat' op invalid input tensor shapes, all input shapes must match except at axis" (MPSGraphUtilities.mm:748) and the process goes down, so the port raises NSInvalidArgumentException where the graph is built. AN AXIS OUTSIDE THE RANK is refused the same way with the release's own words, "invalid axis tensor: [2], axis must be in range -rank <= axis < rank, rank = 2", followed by "LLVM ERROR: Failed to infer result type(s)" taking the process down - refusals.txt's concat-axis-outside and concat-interleave-axis-outside. AN EMPTY ARRAY OF TENSORS IS NOT A REFUSAL AND IS ANSWERED AS THE RELEASE ANSWERS IT, which is what this row said it was not at first: measured over the WHOLE path, `[MPSGraph concatTensors:@[] dimension:0]` BUILDS the result tensor, its shape is NIL and its data type is FLOAT32 (0x10000020), `compileWithDevice:feeds:@{} targetTensors:@[t]` returns an executable, and the run leaves the caller's destination exactly as it was. So the result tensor here carries no shape and no value, and a caller that reads the shape off it gets nil on both sides. graph-cases.m's concat-empty compares those two facts on every run. An earlier text of this row said the port raised NSInvalidArgumentException where the graph is built and called that a deliberate divergence; that was WRONG and is corrected here - an operation the release answers must not take an application down, because the application is one that runs on iOS. MEASURED on this host's own MPSGraph over a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) beside one of (5, 6, 7, 8 | 50, 60, 70, 80) and one of (9, 10, 11, 12 | 90, 100, 110, 120): END TO END along the axis in the order the caller wrote them, so axis 0 of the three is a 6x4 of those three 2x4s one under another and axis 1 a 2x12 of their rows side by side, and a NEGATIVE axis counted from the end (measured: axis -2 answers what axis 0 answers and axis -1 what axis 1 answers, which is the header's own -rank <= dimension < rank). ONE operand is the identity: a 2x4 on its own is a 2x4 of its own eight values. AN EXTENT OF ONE ON THE AXIS LAID ALONG is not a broadcast but one element of the result: measured, a 1x4 of (101, 102, 103, 104) laid along axis 0 beside a 2x4 is a 3x4 of (101, 102, 103, 104 | 5, 6, 7, 8 | 50, 60, 70, 80) and not a 2x4 with the row repeated. THE OPERANDS MAY DIFFER IN LENGTH ON THAT AXIS, and the result is then neither of their lengths: measured, a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) laid along axis 1 beside a 2x1 of (5, 6) is a 2x5 of (1, 2, 3, 4, 10 | 20, 30, 40, 5, 6) - the shorter operand's region is one element of the result, which is graph-cases.m's concat-unequal-axis1. EVERY OTHER AXIS MUST HOLD THE SAME EXTENT IN EVERY OPERAND, which the header calls "broadcast compatible" and the release does not take at all: measured, a 1x4 beside a 2x4 with axis 1 the one laid along is refused by its own compiler with "'mps.concat' op invalid input tensor shapes, all input shapes must match except at axis" (MPSGraphUtilities.mm:748) and the process goes down, so the port raises NSInvalidArgumentException where the graph is built. AN AXIS OUTSIDE THE RANK is refused the same way with the release's own words, "invalid axis tensor: [2], axis must be in range -rank <= axis < rank, rank = 2", followed by "LLVM ERROR: Failed to infer result type(s)" taking the process down - refusals.txt's concat-axis-outside and concat-interleave-axis-outside. AN EMPTY ARRAY OF TENSORS IS NOT A REFUSAL AND IS ANSWERED AS THE RELEASE ANSWERS IT, which is what this row said it was not at first: measured over the WHOLE path, `[MPSGraph concatTensors:@[] dimension:0]` BUILDS the result tensor, its shape is NIL and its data type is FLOAT32 (0x10000020), `compileWithDevice:feeds:@{} targetTensors:@[t]` returns an executable, and the run leaves the caller's destination exactly as it was. So the result tensor here carries no shape and no value, and a caller that reads the shape off it gets nil on both sides. graph-cases.m's concat-empty compares those two facts on every run. An earlier text of this row said the port raised NSInvalidArgumentException where the graph is built and called that a deliberate divergence; that was WRONG and is corrected here - an operation the release answers must not take an application down, because the application is one that runs on iOS. the run's verdict line is "gather_concat checks=37 failures=0 recorded=0" over 742 cells in 38 cases, the red control differing from the release in 38 of the 81 case lines, and facts/MetalPerformanceShadersGraph/Core.md carries every measurement

entries.effect: the same walk as -concatTensors:dimension:name: with the regions of the axis INTERLEAVED, which puts operand i's coordinate c at the result's coordinate i + c * (the number of operands) - so the result's extent on that axis is the sum either way and only which element of the axis each operand's own lands at changes. Measured on this host's own MPSGraph over a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) beside one of (5, 6, 7, 8 | 50, 60, 70, 80) and one of (9, 10, 11, 12 | 90, 100, 110, 120): axis 1 of two is a 2x8 of (1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 7, 4, 8 | 10, 50, 20, 60, 30, 70, 40, 80), axis 1 of three a 2x12 of (1, 5, 9, 2, 6, 10, 3, 7, 11, 4, 8, 12 | 10, 50, 90, 20, 60, 100, 30, 70, 110, 40, 80, 120) and axis 0 of three a 6x4 of the three 2x4s' rows round again - which is the header's own example, concat([operand0, operand1], axis = 0, interleave = YES) = [1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6]. The flag with NO answers EXACTLY what -concatTensors:dimension:name: answers, byte for byte, so it is one bit on one walk and not a second one. The two refusals of that walk are the same two and are named in the row of -concatTensors:dimension:name:, and the interleave form carries the same refusal for an axis outside the rank, measured. SAME refusal for OPERANDS OF DIFFERING LENGTH ON THE AXIS, which is the one form that needs them to agree THERE: measured, a 2x4 beside a 2x1 laid along axis 1 answers a 2x5 end to end (that is concat-unequal-axis1 in the differential) and is REFUSED when they interleave, with the release's own words "'mps.concat' op all input shapes must match along axis dimension when interleaving" (MPSGraphUtilities.mm:748) - refusals.txt's concat-interleave-unequal. That refusal is the whole of the invariant the walk's division by the number of operands rests on, and the port enforces it in its plan rather than per element in its walk; without it the shorter operand is read past its end. MIXED DATA TYPES are the release's COMPILER's refusal and not its graph's: a float32 2x4 beside an int32 2x4 builds a result tensor of shape 2x8 whose data type is the FIRST operand's (0x10000020), and only the compile refuses it, with "'mps.concat' op element type of operand and result differ", the process surviving and writing nothing - refusals.txt's concat-mixed-types. So the result's data type here is the operands' own and the graph carries no type check the release has. AN EMPTY ARRAY IS ANSWERED AS THE RELEASE ANSWERS IT and not refused: measured over the whole path it builds a result tensor of nil shape and float32, the compile returns an executable and the run leaves the caller's destination as it was - graph-cases.m's concat-empty compares the shape and the data type on every run. the run's verdict line is "gather_concat checks=37 failures=0 recorded=0" over 742 cells in 38 cases, the red control differing from the release in 38 of the 81 case lines, and facts/MetalPerformanceShadersGraph/Core.md carries every measurement

entries.effect: the concatenation family with one axis ADDED rather than one axis filled: the result's axis of extent as many operands as the caller wrote down says which operand an element came from, and the axes around it are the operands' own - the one below it is the result's axis below it and the one above it the result's axis one further up. So the result is of the operands' rank plus one, and the axis the caller wrote down is counted from the end of the RESULT's rank, which is the header's own -rank + 1 <= dimension < rank + 1. MEASURED on this host's own MPSGraph over a 2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4 | 10, 20, 30, 40) beside one of (5, 6, 7, 8 | 50, 60, 70, 80): axis 1 is a 2x2x4 of (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 | 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80) and axis 2 a 2x4x2 of (1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 7, 4, 8 | 10, 50, 20, 60, 30, 70, 40, 80), and a negative axis answers what its positive does on that rank (measured: -3, -2 and -1 answer what 0, 1 and 2 answer). ONE operand is the operand itself with the new axis of extent one: measured, a stack of one 2x4 is a 1x2x4 of its own eight values. THE OPERANDS MUST ALL HAVE THE SAME SHAPE, which the header calls "broadcast compatible" and the release does not take: measured, two 2x4s beside a 1x4 stacked at axis 1 are refused by its own compiler with "'mps.concat' op invalid input tensor shapes, all input shapes must match except at axis" (MPSGraphUtilities.mm:748) and so are a 1x4 and a 2x4 stacked at axis 0, and the port raises there instead. AN AXIS OUTSIDE THE RESULT'S RANK is refused with the release's own words and by its own operation - the release builds a stack out of an expanded dimension per operand and then a concatenation, so the expanded dimension names the axis first: "invalid axis: 3, axis must be in range -|rank| <= axis < |rank|" (MPSGraphUtilities.mm:3237), then "LLVM ERROR: Failed to infer result type(s)" takes the process down - refusals.txt's stack-axis-outside and stack-shapes-differ. AN EMPTY ARRAY OF TENSORS IS NOT A REFUSAL AND IS ANSWERED AS THE RELEASE ANSWERS IT, which is what this row said it was not at first: measured over the WHOLE path, `[MPSGraph stackTensors:@[] axis:0]` BUILDS the result tensor, its shape is NIL and its data type is FLOAT32 (0x10000020), the compile returns an executable, and the run leaves the caller's destination exactly as it was. So the result tensor here carries no shape and no value. graph-cases.m's stack-empty compares those two facts on every run. entries.effect: the concatenation family's seam, and the one walk of this library whose result is SEVERAL operands: the operation takes every tensor as an input and the parameters say which axis of the result the operands are laid along, whether they interleave there, and whether that axis is one the operands already have or one the result adds.
